gallery.title: File:Stonewall Jackson Stain Glass.JPG
gallery.description: Stained-glass windows of Stonewall Jackson, until 2017 in the Washington National Cathedral. At left top, Jackson reading the Bible in Confederate camp; left bottom, teaching (using a w:compass (drawing tool)) in w:Virginia Military Institute; bottom right, w:Mexican-American War; upper right, Jackson enters heaven. The windows were removed in 2017.[1]

gallery.title: File:MajGen Paul W. Brier Retirement.jpg
gallery.description: General Joseph F. Dunford, Jr., Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, presenting the Distinguished Service Medal to Paul Brier during his retirement ceremony on February 23, 2019, at the Pentagon.  Brier retired from the Marine Corps after 36 years upon his return from Afghanistan where he had served as Deputy Commander for Civil Outreach and Director, Advise and Assist Directorate, for NATO’s Resolute Support Mission. Subsequent to his this deployment, he had served as Commanding General, 4th Marine Division.

gallery.filename: Guard Tree Monument at the Virginia Military Institute, designed by William Marks Simpson.jpg
gallery.title: File:Guard Tree Monument at the Virginia Military Institute, designed by William Marks Simpson.jpg
gallery.description: The Guard Tree Medallion and Memorial Seat were designed by VMI Art History instructor William Marks Simpson, VMI Class of 1924. The Guard Tree stood on Post from 1839 until the bulk of it was removed due to disease in 1951.

gallery.filename: The Guard Tree Medallion and Memorial Seat were designed by VMI Art History instructor William Marks Simpson VMI Class of 1924..jpg

gallery.description: The Guard Tree Medallion and Memorial Seat were designed by VMI Art History instructor William Marks Simpson VMI Class of 1924. It says “Here Stood the VMI Guard Tree / 1839-1951 / An Emblem of VMI Esteemed by All Her Men." The Guard Tree stood on Post from 1839 until the bulk of it was removed due to disease in 1951.

gallery.title: File:Army 250th Birthday (54590348446).jpg
gallery.artist: U.S. Army Cadet Command (Army ROTC) from Fort Knox, United States
gallery.description: The Army celebrated its 250th birthday on June 14 with a parade in Washington D.C. to honor the history and service of its Soldiers. U.S. Army Cadet Command was represented in the parade by 150 cadets from the Virginia Military Institute, the Citadel, and Texas A&M University who were part of the formation highlighting the future of the Army. Over 6,000 Soldiers participated in the parade that journeyed through the heritage and evolution of the United States Army. | U.S. Army photo by Sarah Windmueller
